mainTopic: Which teaching of רבי יהודה is the source for רב's ruling that an animal slaughtered on שבת is forbidden that day: בררה, broken vessels, separated food, or old lamps?
overview: The גמרא is searching for which teaching of רבי יהודה lies behind רב's ruling that an animal slaughtered on שבת or יום כיפור may not be eaten that day. First it shows that רבי יהודה rejects בררה. The wine case does not prove this, but איו's ברייתא about עירוב does, once רבי יוחנן explains that the חכם had already arrived. Then רב יוסף offers a new source: רבי יהודה's rule that broken vessels may be moved only for a job like their original one, since they were not ready from before שבת. אביי rejects this comparison. A broken vessel is something new (נולד), but meat is just food that was separated, and רבי יהודה permits juice that seeps from fruit meant for eating. The גמרא brings שמואל's teaching about olives and grapes, which would make the animal forbidden. It then notes that רב himself holds that רבי יהודה disagreed even there. Finally רב ששת בריה דרב אידי points to רבי יהודה's ruling on old lamps. The גמרא asks whether that applies to something forbidden because of a prohibition, says yes, and begins a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The wine case has a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the wine case is pushed away. רבי יהודה's concern there is that the wineskin might burst, not a rejection of בררה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is the one taught in the ברייתא. The חכמים said to רבי מאיר: 'Don't you agree that the wineskin might burst, and then it turns out he was drinking untithed wine all along?' He answered them: 'When it bursts, we will worry about it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the earlier proof that רבי יהודה does not hold of בררה. It points to the ברייתא's own stated reason for the stricter opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ones who forbid drinking the wine are worried that the wineskin will burst before the תרומה is separated. The man would then have been drinking טבל. That is a practical worry, not a statement that בררה does not work, so the case proves nothing about בררה.

keyTerms.meaning: retroactively, looking back to the start
produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been taken
a leather wineskin
when it bursts

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה is shown here to accept בררה. The גמרא only says this case does not prove he rejects it, because his reason here is a different one.

phrases.english: There, the reason is as it is taught:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the earlier case of a man drinking wine and planning to separate תרומה from it afterward.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Meir:
"Don't you agree
that perhaps the wineskin will burst,
and it will turn out he was drinking untithed produce all along?"
He said to them: "When it bursts."
phrases.notes: He means: we don't worry about it until it actually happens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the wine case that the גמרא brought just before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the wine case. The question of רבי יהודה's view stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The strict view in that case comes from the worry that the wineskin will burst, not from rejecting בררה.

steps.title: A new proof from איו's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the wine proof and says the source is a ברייתא taught by איו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from what איו teaches.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to bring a new source to show that רבי יהודה does not accept בררה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the previous proof failed, so a different one is needed. The actual text of איו's ברייתא comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; the earlier attempt is dropped and a new one is offered
the idea that a later choice clarifies what was meant from the start

phrases.english: Rather, it is from what Ayo teaches.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves this part unsaid: it's from this teaching that we learn רבי יהודה does not accept בררה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the wine proof, the גמרא turns to a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds אין בררה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא taught by איו about עירוב תחומין.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's rule on a two-way עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a person may make his עירוב depend on which direction the חכם comes. He may not leave it open to go in whichever direction he himself decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: As איו teaches: רבי יהודה says a person cannot set a condition on two things as one. Rather, if the חכם comes to the east, his עירוב is to the east, and if to the west, his עירוב is to the west. But 'to here or to there' does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes איו's ברייתא. In it רבי יהודה allows one kind of two-sided condition for an עירוב and forbids another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It works if the עירוב depends on where the חכם comes, east or west. It does not work if the person keeps both options open to choose later, 'here or there.' The גמרא wants to read this refusal as רבי יהודה rejecting בררה.

keyTerms.meaning: sets a condition
two things at once, both options together
his עירוב תחומין, food placed to extend where he may walk on שבת
to here or to there, whichever he picks

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve east and west. The difference is who decides: in the allowed case it depends on where the חכם comes, and in the forbidden case the person picks freely.

phrases.english: As Ayo teaches: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A person may not set a condition
on two matters as one,
rather, if a Sage comes to the east,
his eruv is to the east;
to the west, his eruv is to the west;
whereas to here or to there, no.
phrases.notes: He means: an עירוב set up so he can go whichever way he wants does not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the text of the source announced in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב that depends on where the חכם comes works. An עירוב left open to 'here or there' by the person's own later choice does not work.

steps.title: Why should east-or-west work either?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls its old question on this ברייתא. If 'here or there' fails because of אין בררה, east-or-west should fail too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What is different about 'here or there' that it does not work? Because there is no בררה? Then east-or-west also has no בררה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty on איו's ברייתא. It asks why רבי יהודה treats the two cases differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases, which עירוב counts is decided only later on שבת. So if the reason 'here or there' fails is אין בררה, the east-or-west condition depends on בררה just as much and should also fail. The ברייתא seems to contradict itself.

keyTerms.meaning: and we discussed it; we raised a question on it before
what is the difference?
a later choice cannot clarify what was meant from the start
also

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer to this question will show what רבי יהודה really holds about בררה, and that is the whole point of bringing this source.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What is different about 'to here or to there'
that it does not work? Because there is no retroactive clarification?
East or west also has no retroactive clarification!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא לְכָאן וּלְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the internal logic of the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's distinction in איו's ברייתא between east-or-west and 'here or there'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both conditions are settled only later, so both rely on בררה. If אין בררה rules out one, it should rule out the other too.

steps.title: The Sage had already arrived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the question from step 4: in the east-or-west case the חכם had already come before the condition was made, so the עירוב does not depend on בררה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: this is talking about a case where the חכם had already arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question on איו's ברייתא. East-or-west works because the matter was already settled when the person made his condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if 'here or there' fails because of אין בררה, east-or-west should fail too. רבי יוחנן answers that by the time the person set his condition, the חכם had already come to one side. The person just did not know which side, so nothing is being decided later and no בררה is needed. This saves the ברייתא and confirms that רבי יהודה rejects בררה. Even so, the next step drops this whole line and looks for a different source for רב's ruling about the slaughtered animal.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sage had already come; the outcome was already fixed
Deciding later and treating it as if it was set from the start

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is a case where the Sage had already come.
phrases.notes: He means the חכם was already in the east or the west when the condition was made. The person just didn't know which.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּכְבָר בָּא חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by defining the east-or-west case narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: East-or-west depends on a future event, so it should need בררה just like 'here or there'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכם had already arrived, so the outcome was fixed and only unknown to the person. No בררה is needed.

steps.title: A new source: רבי יהודה on broken vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רב's 'רבי יהודה' refers to רבי יהודה's view on vessels. He begins quoting the משנה about moving broken pieces of vessels on שבת, starting with the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: it is רבי יהודה's view on vessels. As the משנה teaches: all vessels that may be moved on שבת, their broken pieces may also be moved, as long as they can do some kind of job. Pieces of a large bowl can cover the mouth of a barrel. Pieces of glass can cover the mouth of a flask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the עירוב approach and gives a brand-new source for רבי יהודה. Here it quotes the first half of the משנה to set up the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the עירוב approach is being dropped. רב יוסף points to the laws of מוקצה with broken vessels. The תנא קמא is lenient: broken pieces may be moved if they can do any useful job at all, even a completely new one like covering a barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier approach and brings a new one
Broken pieces of vessels
Some kind of useful work, any job at all
A large bowl, such as a kneading trough
A small flask or jug

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
It is the view of Rabbi Yehuda regarding vessels,
phrases.notes: When רב said the animal is forbidden 'according to רבי יהודה', he meant this view about vessels.

phrases.english: as we learned in a Mishnah:
All vessels that may be moved on Shabbat,
their broken pieces may be moved,
as long as they can do some kind of work.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְרֵי עֲרֵיבָה – לְכַסּוֹת בָּהֶן פִּי חָבִית,
phrases.english: Pieces of a large bowl: to cover the mouth of a barrel with them;

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְרֵי זְכוּכִית – לְכַסּוֹת בָּהֶן פִּי הַפַּךְ.
phrases.english: pieces of glass: to cover the mouth of a flask with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּכֵלִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בררה line, which did not explain why the slaughtered animal is forbidden that day, and brings a new source from the laws of vessels on שבת.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that an animal slaughtered on שבת is forbidden that day according to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שבת 124b about broken vessels.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only a job like the original one
steps.stepSummary: In the same משנה, רבי יהודה is stricter. The pieces may be moved only if they can do a job similar to what the vessel did before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: only if they can do a job like their own original job. Bowl pieces must be able to hold thick stew poured into them. Glass pieces must be able to hold oil poured into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with רבי יהודה's stricter opinion. This is the key line the proof will be built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a one-word change: the תנא קמא says מלאכה, any job, and רבי יהודה says מלאכתן, their own job. A bowl held food, so its piece must still hold food. Covering a barrel is a new job, and that is not enough for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Work similar to their own original use
A thick stew or porridge
To pour into them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't miss the small difference: מְלָאכָה means any job, while מְלַאכְתָּן means their own job. The whole proof depends on this one word.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
as long as they can do work similar to their own work;
pieces of a large bowl: to pour thick stew into them;
pieces of glass: to pour oil into them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהוּ עוֹשִׂין מֵעֵין מְלַאכְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה with רבי יהודה's dissent from the תנא קמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Broken pieces may be moved on שבת only if they can serve a function similar to their original use.

steps.title: Not prepared from yesterday means forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference: for רבי יהודה, something not ready before שבת for its current use is forbidden. The same applies to an animal slaughtered on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A job like their own job: yes. A different kind of job: no. So we see that since the pieces were not ready from yesterday for this new job, they are forbidden. Here too, since the animal was not ready from yesterday, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pulls a general rule out of רבי יהודה's words and applies it to the slaughtered animal. This is his proposed source for רב's ruling, and אביי challenges it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שבת the pieces were part of a whole vessel, so they were never set aside for a new job like covering a barrel. That is why רבי יהודה forbids them. A live animal before שבת was not ready to be eaten either. Slaughtering it on שבת makes it ready only on that day, so it stays forbidden for that day.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently; we see from here
Was prepared from yesterday, ready before the holy day began
Here too; applying the same rule to our case
Something set apart and not ready for use on שבת, so it is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's proposed source for רבי יהודה is broken vessels: what was not ready before שבת for its present use is forbidden that day. אביי will argue that this does not fit an animal slaughtered on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the whole discussion from בררה to the rule of 'not prepared from yesterday', which is the basis of מוקצה. That rule now explains רב's ruling about the slaughtered animal.

phrases.english: Similar to their own work: yes;
similar to a different kind of work: no.
Apparently, since they were not prepared from yesterday
for this work, they are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אִיתְּכַן מֵאֶתְמוֹל – אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: Here too, since it was not prepared from yesterday, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the animal slaughtered on שבת or יום כיפור. Before the day began it was alive, so it wasn't ready to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעֵין מְלַאכְתָּן – אִין, מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה אַחֶרֶת – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from רבי יהודה's wording in step 7 and applies it to the slaughtered animal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יהודה, whatever was not prepared before the day for its present use is forbidden that day. So an animal slaughtered on שבת is forbidden to eat that day.

steps.title: אביי: a broken vessel is not like slaughtered meat
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's comparison. A broken vessel turned into something new, but an animal was food before and is still food.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are these cases really the same? There, it started out as a vessel and now it is a broken piece of a vessel. So it is something newly created (נולד), and it is forbidden. Here, it started out as food and in the end it is food. It is just food that was separated.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues that רב יוסף's proof from broken vessels does not fit the case of an animal slaughtered on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel that breaks changes its identity: it was a כלי and now it is a שבר כלי, a new thing that was not ready before שבת. An animal was always seen as food, and slaughter only separates the meat so you can eat it. Nothing new was created, so the reason for forbidding broken vessels does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? A phrase used to reject a comparison
A broken piece of a vessel
Something newly created on שבת, which was not ready before שבת, so it is forbidden
Food that was separated: food that was always food, only now detached

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying broken vessels are permitted for רבי יהודה. He agrees they are forbidden. He is only saying meat is a different kind of case.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Are they comparable?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב יוסף, who brought the proof from the broken vessels in step 6.

phrases.english: There, at first it was a vessel,
and now it is a broken piece of a vessel,
so it is something newly created, and it is forbidden.
Here, at first it was food,
phrases.notes: Even while the animal was alive, it was seen as food.

phrases.english: and in the end it is food,
it is just food that was separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 8 by showing that the broken-vessel case is not comparable.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's proof from broken vessels to an animal slaughtered on שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A broken vessel is a new thing (נולד), but slaughtered meat is the same food as before, only separated.

steps.title: אביי's source: fruit juice that seeps out on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי claims רבי יהודה permits 'food that was separated' and begins quoting a משנה about squeezing fruit. First he gives the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we know that רבי יהודה holds that food that was separated is permitted. As we learned in a משנה: One may not squeeze fruit to get liquid out of it. And if the liquid came out by itself, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets up his proof. He starts quoting a משנה, and this part is only the first opinion. רבי יהודה's view comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Squeezing fruit on שבת is forbidden. The תנא קמא adds that even juice that seeped out by itself is forbidden. This sets the background so we can see how רבי יהודה disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine, it is permitted
Squeezing (fruit to get its juice)
Liquids, juice
Came out by themselves, without squeezing

phrases.english: And we have heard that רבי יהודה says:
food that was separated is permitted,
as we learned: One may not squeeze fruit
to get liquids out of them,
and if they came out by themselves, they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: ושמעינן ליה לרבי יהודה דאמר אוכלא דאיפרת שפיר דמי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support אביי's claim from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה permits אוכלא דאיפרת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת about juice seeping out of fruit

steps.title: רבי יהודה: juice from eating-fruit is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the fruit was meant for eating, juice that came out is permitted. If it was meant for juice, the juice is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If the fruit was meant for eating, what comes out of it is permitted. If it was meant for liquids, what comes out of it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי יהודה's view in the same משנה, which is the heart of אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the fruit was meant for eating, the juice is seen as part of the food that just separated, so it is permitted. אביי's point is that slaughtered meat should be the same: food that was separated, so it should be permitted for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Meant for eating
Meant for making juice
What comes out of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the clearest example of אוכלא דאיפרת being permitted. It is the base of אביי's argument that רבי יהודה would allow an animal slaughtered on שבת.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: If they were meant for eating,
what comes out of them is permitted,
and if they were meant for liquids, what comes out of them is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהודה אומר אם לאוכלין היוצא מהן מותר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote of the משנה begun in step 10 with רבי יהודה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Juice that seeps from fruit meant for eating is permitted; from fruit meant for juice it is forbidden.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה agrees about olives and grapes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof: שמואל taught that רבי יהודה agrees with the חכמים to forbid juice from baskets of olives and grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about this משנה: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי יהודה agreed with the חכמים in the case of baskets of olives and grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions אביי's proof from the juice משנה by bringing a limit on רבי יהודה's leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olives and grapes are normally used for their oil and wine. So even if someone planned to eat them, רבי יהודה forbids the liquid that comes out. This shows רבי יהודה does not permit every case of separated food, so the proof that he would permit an animal slaughtered on שבת is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it said about it? Brings a later teaching on the משנה
Agrees (with the other opinion)
Baskets of olives and grapes

phrases.english: Wasn't it said about it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the juice משנה that אביי just quoted.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
רבי יהודה agreed with the חכמים
in the case of baskets of olives and grapes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לאו אתמר עלה אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against אביי's proof from steps 10-11 by limiting רבי יהודה's leniency.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's proof that רבי יהודה permits all אוכלא דאיפרת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה forbids liquid from olives and grapes even when meant for eating, so his leniency is limited and does not clearly cover an animal slaughtered on שבת.

steps.title: Olives and grapes are like an animal ready for slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the push-back from שמואל: the juice is forbidden because the person has his mind on squeezing, and the same is true of an animal meant for slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that since olives and grapes are meant for squeezing, the owner has his mind on their juice. Here too, since the animal is meant for slaughter, the owner has his mind on eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל's teaching (Step 12) knocks down אביי's proof, and it applies the same reasoning to the slaughtered animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olives and grapes are normally squeezed, so the owner thinks of them as juice. If the juice were allowed, he might come to squeeze on שבת. An animal is normally slaughtered, so the same worry applies: allowing the meat could lead him to slaughter on שבת. So even רבי יהודה would forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see / this shows that
They stand ready for squeezing
He sets his mind on it, he is thinking of using it
Here too, the same applies in our case

phrases.english: So we see, since they stand ready for squeezing –
he sets his mind on them;
phrases.notes: He is already thinking of their juice. If the juice were allowed, he might squeeze them on שבת.

phrases.english: here too, since it stands ready for slaughter –
he sets his mind on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in Step 12 by drawing out its reasoning and applying it to the animal.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's proof from the juice case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Olives and grapes are meant for squeezing, just as an animal is meant for slaughter. So the case actually supports forbidding the animal.

steps.title: But רב himself holds רבי יהודה permits even olives and grapes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the whole question comes from רב, and רב holds that רבי יהודה disagreed even about baskets of olives and grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there any question at all, except according to רב? And רב said: רבי יהודה disagreed even about baskets of olives and grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the argument from שמואל in Step 13 cannot help explain רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole discussion started because רב said that forbidding the slaughtered animal follows רבי יהודה. But רב himself holds that רבי יהודה permits juice even from olives and grapes. So according to רב, the juice case points toward permitting the animal, and we still need another source for רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there any reason or issue other than this
Disagreed
Baskets of olives and grapes, which are meant for squeezing

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל and רב disagree about what רבי יהודה held. Since this is רב's ruling, the גמרא must explain it using רב's own view, not שמואל's.

phrases.english: Is there any question at all, except according to רב?
phrases.notes: The whole question started because רב said the ruling about the slaughtered animal follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: But רב said:
רבי יהודה disagreed
even regarding baskets of olives and grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 13's reasoning as a way to explain רב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using שמואל's teaching to explain רב's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב holds that רבי יהודה permits juice even from olives and grapes, so this reasoning does not fit רב.

steps.title: רב meant רבי יהודה's ruling about lamps
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי says רב was referring to רבי יהודה's ruling that an old lamp may not be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת son of רב אידי said: it is the רבי יהודה of lamps. As we learned: one may move a new lamp, but not an old one. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer: רב's ruling comes from a different teaching of רבי יהודה, the one about old lamps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that an old, dirty lamp is set aside from use when שבת begins, so it stays forbidden to move for all of שבת. In the same way, the animal was forbidden to eat when שבת began, since a living animal may not be eaten, so it stays forbidden all שבת even after it is slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: One may move or carry an object
A new, unused clay lamp
An old lamp covered with oil and soot

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rather, רב ששת son of רב אידי said:
It is the רבי יהודה of lamps,
phrases.notes: He means רב was thinking of רבי יהודה's ruling about lamps, not the juice ruling.

phrases.english: as it was taught: One may move a new lamp,
but not an old one,
phrases.notes: An old lamp is dirty and disgusting, so a person puts it out of his mind for all of שבת.

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new source for רב's ruling after Step 14 ruled out the juice case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling was based on רבי יהודה's view about separated juice.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ruling is based on רבי יהודה's view about old lamps: what was set aside when שבת began stays set aside all שבת.

steps.title: Disgusting is not the same as forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lamp comparison: the lamp is set aside because it is disgusting, while the animal is set aside because of a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say you heard רבי יהודה rule this about something set aside because it is disgusting. Did you hear him say it about something set aside because of a prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the lamp case really matches the slaughtered animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person keeps away from an old lamp because he finds it disgusting, so he has truly put it out of his mind. The animal was off-limits only because of a prohibition, since it was alive. Maybe רבי יהודה is strict only in the first kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, grant that
Set aside because it is disgusting
Set aside because of a halachic prohibition

phrases.english: Say that you heard רבי יהודה rule this
about something set aside because it is disgusting,

phrases.aramaic: מוּקְצֶה מֵחֲמַת אִיסּוּר מִי שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: but something set aside because of a prohibition, did you hear him rule that?
phrases.notes: That is our animal: before it was slaughtered, it was off-limits because of a prohibition, not because it was disgusting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי's comparison of the animal to the old lamp
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lamp is set aside because it is disgusting, while the animal is set aside because of a prohibition. So רבי יהודה's strictness may not carry over.

steps.title: Yes, and here is the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה does hold this for something set aside because of a prohibition, and begins quoting a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as we learned: רבי יהודה says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with 'yes' and is setting up a quote from רבי יהודה that will prove it. The quote itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא claims that רבי יהודה is also strict about something set aside because of a prohibition. If the coming source proves this, the lamp comparison works and רב's ruling can follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

phrases.english: Yes, as we learned:
רבי יהודה says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16's challenge and begins the supporting source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה is strict even about something set aside because of a prohibition
